verdicts.reason: OrganizationMember.has_global_access is `models.BooleanField(default=True)` and is copied verbatim into RpcOrganizationMember by organizations/services/organization/serial.py:47, so the `enable_advanced` gate is satisfied by ordinary org members, not just administrators as the added comments assert.

verdicts.evidence: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:441-452 (removed block); repo-wide grep for segment_span_count_exceeded
verdicts.reason: The in-repo half checks out: `spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded` was deleted from _load_segment_data and now has zero references anywhere in the tree. Whether a dashboard or alert still consumes it cannot be settled here; it would take a grep of the sentry ops/dashboard definitions, which live outside this repository.

Both halves check out: has_global_access defaults to True on OrganizationMember, and `request.user.is_superuser` is the raw User model column while the rest of the codebase (including OrganizationAuditPermission at api/bases/organization.py:124) gates on is_active_superuser(request), which additionally requires an active superuser session.

The core assertion is right: `member: RpcOrganizationMember | None` and the endpoint dereferences it unguarded, so member=None raises AttributeError. The stated trigger is wrong, though: for an actual superuser `request.user.is_superuser` is True and Python's `or` short-circuits before the dereference; the crash is reached by non-superuser callers with no membership (token auth), not by superusers.

In the pinned sentry-kafka-schemas==1.3.6, SpanEvent declares `end_timestamp_precise: Required["_PositiveFloat"]`, so the premise of the question is false and the direct index in factory.py:141 is consistent with the schema (and with existing direct indexing in spans/consumers/process_segments/message.py).

Both zunionstore calls omit AGGREGATE, so Redis sums scores for members present in both inputs. Redelivery of a span (the pipeline is at-least-once; buffer.py:459 already logs duplicate-segment fallout) re-populates the parent key with a payload already present in the redirect target, and the union then stores 2x the end timestamp, corrupting the ordering the zpopmin eviction at line 63 relies on.

AuditLogQueryParamSerializer is constructed from request.GET and declares only `event` and `actor`; DRF ignores unknown fields, and line 70 reads `optimized_pagination` straight off request.GET with an exact `== "true"` comparison, so `True`/`1`/`TRUE` silently disable the feature rather than 400.

Verified with `grep -n ' $'`: trailing whitespace on organization_auditlogs.py lines 72 and 89 and paginator.py lines 824/827/829, plus three blank lines before `class OptimizedCursorPaginator` and a trailing blank line at EOF — all of which `ruff format --check` normalizes.

Nothing enforces that the root span holds the maximum end_timestamp_precise — zpopmin evicts purely by score — and the span-buf:hrs: key is only ever set (lua:69) or deleted in done_flush_segments (buffer.py:470). So an evicted root leaves has_root_span=1 and the segment keeps the shorter span_buffer_root_timeout_secs deadline; the claimed guarantee does not exist in the code.

The key format string `span-buf:s:{...}:{...}` is byte-for-byte unchanged while sadd/scard/sunionstore/sscan all became zadd/zcard/zunionstore/zscan, and there is no version suffix or migration anywhere in the diff. Every span-buf:s: key still live at deploy (redis_ttl is 3600s) will answer the new z* commands with WRONGTYPE.

A repo-wide grep for max_segment_spans returns only the __init__ default (1001) and the self-assignment; the sole reader was the block removed from _load_segment_data. The Lua cap is the literal 1000, so the two numbers disagree and the Python one is now unreachable.

OptimizedCursorPaginator copies Paginator.value_from_cursor (`return cursor.value`) while being used with order_by='-datetime'; DateTimePaginator instead converts via datetime.fromtimestamp(value/1000). build_queryset then emits `extra(where=['"datetime" <= %s'], params=[<number>])` against a timestamptz column, which Postgres rejects.

`git show <base>` confirms the loop was `for i = 0, 10000 do  -- theoretically this limit means that segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly.` and is now `for i = 0, 1000 do` with the comment gone; the PR description is about eviction and says nothing about a 10x reduction in redirect-chain resolution depth.

The `else offset` arm of the new conditional passes cursor.offset through unclamped, so an is_prev cursor with a negative offset reaches `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start and Django 5.2 raises ValueError('Negative indexing is not supported.'). Wording is loose — BasePaginator has clamping rather than an explicit negative-offset branch — and this crash path pre-dates the PR (the base used bare `offset`), but the diff rewrites exactly this line without fixing it.

Accurate: Cursor.from_string accepts a negative middle field, and the new expression only clamps when `not cursor.is_prev`, so `?cursor=<v>:-5:1` still slices with a negative start. One nit — Django 5.2's QuerySet.__getitem__ raises ValueError rather than asserting — and this particular crash existed before the PR too; what the diff changes is that the non-prev half now silently swallows it.

Confirmed: the eviction threshold is the literal 1000 in Lua while SpansBuffer still takes max_segment_spans=1001, and nothing passes that value to the script, so any caller configuring it is silently ignored and the effective cap is off by one from the documented one.

Correct including the regression framing: `enable_advanced` is computed unconditionally, before the `if use_optimized` test, so it runs on every GET. OrgAuthTokenAuthentication/ApiKeyAuthentication are in DEFAULT_AUTHENTICATION and authenticate with user=None, and ControlSiloOrganizationEndpoint.convert_args resolves the context with that user id, leaving member=None — AttributeError, 500, on a path that previously worked.

get_item_key is copied from Paginator (int/floor/ceil) but the endpoint constructs the paginator with order_by='-datetime', so `value` is a datetime.datetime; math.floor/math.ceil have no __floor__/__ceil__ for datetime and raise TypeError. build_cursor calls key() on every non-empty result set, so the endpoint 500s on the first request that returns any row.

Same finding as c011/c016 and equally verified: max_segment_spans is assigned and never read after the _load_segment_data block was deleted, and the real limit is the hardcoded 1000 in the Lua script.

BasePaginator.get_result is inherited by Paginator, DateTimePaginator and friends across the whole API, so clamping the non-prev offset to 0 changes every cursor-paginated endpoint: a negative offset that previously blew up in Django's slice now silently returns the offset-0 page with no signal to the caller, and the commit that does it is titled feat(audit-logs) and adds no paginator tests. (Minor imprecision: with a non-empty cursor value it returns the value-anchored page at offset 0, not literally page one.)

The header ARGS list is genuinely out of sync with the body — it lists payload first while ARGV[1] is is_root_span — but `git show <base>` shows the header was already stale before this PR and the diff does not touch it. The claim's causal explanation is also off: payload was inserted from Python by sadd before the change, not newly moved out by zadd.

The removed block did exactly what the claim says (metrics.incr + logger.error + drop the whole segment), and its replacement is a bare `redis.call('zpopmin', set_key, span_count - 1000)` that returns nothing to Python — the script's return value is unchanged at {redirect_depth, span_key, set_key, has_root_span} — so evictions are invisible. Eviction is by end timestamp only, with no regard for parent/child links.

verdicts.evidence: tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py (6 tests, none exceeding a handful of spans); tests/sentry/api/endpoints/test_organization_auditlogs.py
verdicts.reason: The only test changes in the spans commit add end_timestamp_precise to existing fixtures; no test builds a segment past the 1000-span cap or asserts anything about eviction. The audit-log commit (8ab88145) touches three src files and no tests, and test_organization_auditlogs.py never sends optimized_pagination.

Same defect as c006 with the consequence spelled out, and the direction is right: SUM roughly doubles the score of a duplicated member, and since zpopmin removes the lowest scores that member becomes the last thing evicted while legitimately newer spans go first.

The branch assigns `start_offset = cursor.offset` when it is negative and slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]`; Django 5.2's QuerySet.__getitem__ raises ValueError('Negative indexing is not supported.') for any negative slice start, so the inline comment claiming the ORM 'properly handles negative slicing automatically' is false and the advertised feature can only 500.
